title: Unique infinitesimal lifting for etale algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:E\to Y$ be etale, meaning that its maps on etale scheme charts are etale morphisms of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a first order thickening of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. For morphisms $b:T\to Y$ and $e_0:T_0\to E$ with $p e_0=b i$, there is exactly one $e:T\to E$ with $e i=e_0$ and $p e=b$.

source.place: Tag 0616 (lemma-etale-formally-etale), implication (1) to (2), and Tag 04GC (definition-formally-etale), using definition-formally-smooth-etale-unramified. Only the affine square-zero lifting assertion is used.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary compatible etale chart diagram $v h=p u$ with $U,V$ schemes. By the chartwise etaleness hypothesis on $p$, the scheme morphism $h:U\to V$ is etale. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $h$ is flat and unramified (as well as locally of finite presentation). Only the first two properties will be needed.

source.place: Tag 02HM (lemma-etale-formally-etale), proof of (1) implies (2), first two sentences.

proof.text: For any first order thickening $j:Z_0\hookrightarrow Z$ of affine $S$-schemes and any square $h c_0=dj$ with $c_0:Z_0\to U$, $d:Z\to V$, regard $Z$ as a scheme over the scheme $V$ via $d$, and $Z_0$ via $dj$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] to $h$ with this base $V$ and the flatness and unramifiedness from step 1. It gives exactly one $c:Z\to U$ over $V$ restricting to $c_0$. Such $c$ is an $S$-morphism since $h$ and $d$ are $S$-morphisms. Thus $P(h)$, in the notation of [lem-sfb-formally-etale-space-chart-locality], holds for every compatible chart diagram.

The reverse implication of [lem-sfb-formally-etale-space-chart-locality] now yields $P(p)$ from step 2. Substitute $T_0,T,i,e_0,b$ from the statement in the definition of $P(p)$. Its unique morphism $e:T\to E$ satisfies precisely $e i=e_0$ and $p e=b$, proving both existence and uniqueness.
